No se asume que EQG mejora HIS.\n","metadata":{}},{"id":"03c2b8be-8310-4544-979f-f13c06874d68","cell_type":"code","source":"import json, math\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Tuple, List, Dict\nimport numpy as np\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\nnp.random.seed(42)\nOUT = Path(\"/kaggle/working/his_preqpu\") if Path(\"/kaggle/working\").exists() else Path(\"his_preqpu\")\nOUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\nEPS = 1e-8\nN_BOOT = 400\n\ndef HIS(h_id: float, h_re: float, eps: float = EPS) -> float:\n    d = abs(h_id)\n    if d < eps:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return 1.0 - abs(h_id - h_re) / d\n\ndef HRF(his_e, his_a, eps=EPS):\n    if abs(his_a) < eps or math.isnan(his_a) or math.isnan(his_e):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return his_e / his_a\n\nprint(\"HIS pre-QPU extension  boot=%d\" % N_BOOT)\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.257222Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.258340Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.271358Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.258302Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.270385Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"HIS pre-QPU extension  boot=400\n","output_type":"stream"}],"execution_count":37},{"id":"43317b87-6446-41f1-9ec5-df23052868d3","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 1. Incertidumbre formal de HIS\n\nSi $\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{re}}$ se estima con error estandar $\\mathrm{SE}_H$ (p.ej. por shots),\npor el metodo delta:\n\n$$\n\\mathrm{SE}(\\mathrm{HIS}) \\approx \\frac{\\mathrm{SE}_H}{|\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{id}}|}\n\\quad\\text{(cuando el signo de }\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{id}}-\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{re}}\\text{ es estable)}.\n$$\n\nAdemas: bootstrap no parametrico sobre estimaciones de $\\langle H\\rangle_{\\mathrm{re}}$.\nContraste E−A: $z = \\Delta\\mathrm{HIS}/\\sqrt{\\mathrm{SE}_E^2+\\mathrm{SE}_A^2}$.\n","metadata":{}},{"id":"6e57dc93-5451-4ee3-8851-8d8a1fd3f06c","cell_type":"code","source":"def se_his_delta(h_id: float, se_h_re: float, eps: float = EPS) -> float:\n    d = abs(h_id)\n    if d < eps:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return se_h_re / d\n\ndef his_bootstrap(h_id: float, h_re_samples: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[float, float, Tuple[float, float]]:\n    \"\"\"Return mean HIS, SE, 95% CI from bootstrap sample of <H>_real.\"\"\"\n    vals = np.array([HIS(h_id, x) for x in h_re_samples], dtype=float)\n    vals = vals[~np.isnan(vals)]\n    if len(vals) < 2:\n        return float(\"nan\"), float(\"nan\"), (float(\"nan\"), float(\"nan\"))\n    mu = float(np.mean(vals))\n    se = float(np.std(vals, ddof=1) / np.sqrt(len(vals)))\n    lo, hi = np.percentile(vals, [2.5, 97.5])\n    return mu, se, (float(lo), float(hi))\n\ndef z_delta(his1, se1, his2, se2):\n    se = math.sqrt(se1**2 + se2**2)\n    if se < EPS or math.isnan(se):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return (his1 - his2) / se\n\n# Demo analitica\nh_id = 1.85\nh_re = 1.40\nse_h = 0.05\nhis = HIS(h_id, h_re)\nse = se_his_delta(h_id, se_h)\nprint(\"Ejemplo: H_id=%.3f H_re=%.3f SE_H=%.3f -> HIS=%.4f  SE(HIS)~%.4f\" % (h_id, h_re, se_h, his, se))\nprint(\"CI95 approx: [%.4f, %.4f]\" % (his - 1.96*se, his + 1.96*se))\n\n# Bootstrap demo\nsamples = h_re + se_h * np.random.randn(N_BOOT)\nmu, se_b, ci = his_bootstrap(h_id, samples)\nprint(\"Bootstrap: HIS=%.4f SE=%.4f CI95=[%.4f, %.4f]\" % (mu, se_b, ci[0], ci[1]))\nprint(\"PASSED: SE/CI/z definidos para publicacion\")\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.272955Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.273304Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.298146Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.273275Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.296823Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"Ejemplo: H_id=1.850 H_re=1.400 SE_H=0.050 -> HIS=0.7568  SE(HIS)~0.0270\nCI95 approx: [0.7038, 0.8097]\nBootstrap: HIS=0.7574 SE=0.0013 CI95=[0.7090, 0.8133]\nPASSED: SE/CI/z definidos para publicacion\n","output_type":"stream"}],"execution_count":38},{"id":"fea09a48-9f1c-43d2-9980-3c180b7e1d4a","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 2. Independencia HIS vs AR (simulaciones ruidosas)\n\n**Pregunta:** si $\\mathrm{corr}(\\mathrm{HIS},\\mathrm{AR})\\approx 1$, HIS no aporta dimension nueva.\n\nModelo: Ising MaxCut path $n=4$, estado de referencia fijo, ruido = depolarizing de $p_j$.\nAR se define respecto al corte optimo del path (coste = numero de aristas cortadas / 3).\nHIS usa $\\langle H\\rangle$ del mismo $H$ Ising. Ambos se degradan con ruido, pero no tienen por que ser colineales si la masa de probabilidad se redistribuye de formas distintas.\n","metadata":{}},{"id":"e5c819a2-d462-4ee6-bb22-1f9d42b7f1b1","cell_type":"code","source":"# MaxCut path n=4: edges (0,1),(1,2),(2,3) — optimal cut value = 3\n# H = sum_edges 0.5*(I - Z_i Z_j)  => <H> = expected cut value\nn = 4\nd = 1 << n\nedges = [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3)]\n\ndef cut_value(bit: int) -> int:\n    c = 0\n    for i, j in edges:\n        bi = (bit >> i) & 1\n        bj = (bit >> j) & 1\n        c += int(bi != bj)\n    return c\n\nlam = np.array([float(cut_value(x)) for x in range(d)])  # eigenvalues = cut values\nopt = float(lam.max())  # 3.0\n\n# reference distribution: favor high-cut states but not only optimal\np0 = np.zeros(d)\nfor x in range(d):\n    p0[x] = math.exp(1.2 * (lam[x] - opt))\np0 /= p0.sum()\n\ndef depolarize(p, q):\n    return (1 - q) * p + q / d\n\ndef AR_from_p(p):\n    # Approximation ratio = expected cut / opt\n    return float(np.dot(p, lam) / opt)\n\ndef H_from_p(p):\n    return float(np.dot(p, lam))\n\nh_id = H_from_p(p0)\nassert abs(h_id) >= EPS\nar_id = AR_from_p(p0)\n\nqs = np.linspace(0, 0.9, 40)\nhis_s, ar_s = [], []\nfor q in qs:\n    p = depolarize(p0, q)\n    his_s.append(HIS(h_id, H_from_p(p)))\n    ar_s.append(AR_from_p(p))\n\nhis_s = np.array(his_s)\nar_s = np.array(ar_s)\ncorr = float(np.corrcoef(his_s, ar_s)[0, 1])\nprint(\"<H>_id=%.4f  AR_id=%.4f  opt=%.1f\" % (h_id, ar_id, opt))\nprint(\"corr(HIS, AR) sobre barrido depolarizing = %.4f\" % corr)\n\n# Segundo escenario: ruido que mueve masa entre estados de MISMO corte\n# (AR casi fija localmente) vs HIS si hubiera terminos no-diagonal — aqui H es diagonal\n# en cut basis, AR y <H> son proporcionalmente ligados: AR = <H>/opt, HIS = 1 - |1 - <H>_re/<H>_id|\n# => en H Ising diagonal puro, HIS y AR estan funcionalmente relacionados.\n# Demostramos eso y luego un H con terminos off-diagonal donde se desacoplan.\n\nprint(\"\\nNota: para H Ising DIAGONAL en base computacional, <H> = opt*AR\")\nprint(\"  => HIS = 1 - |h_id - opt*AR|/|h_id|  esta ligado a AR.\")\nprint(\"  corr alta en este caso es ESPERABLE, no prueba de redundancia universal.\")\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.299579Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.299993Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.332492Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.299957Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.331252Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"<H>_id=2.3056  AR_id=0.7685  opt=3.0\ncorr(HIS, AR) sobre barrido depolarizing = 1.0000\n\nNota: para H Ising DIAGONAL en base computacional, <H> = opt*AR\n  => HIS = 1 - |h_id - opt*AR|/|h_id|  esta ligado a AR.\n  corr alta en este caso es ESPERABLE, no prueba de redundancia universal.\n","output_type":"stream"}],"execution_count":39},{"id":"a60c8836-9e22-4665-8751-7b0364e5227a","cell_type":"code","source":"# H con terminos X/Y: <H> ya no es funcion lineal del AR de MaxCut\nPAULI = {\n    \"I\": np.array([[1, 0], [0, 1]], complex),\n    \"X\": np.array([[0, 1], [1, 0]], complex),\n    \"Y\": np.array([[0, -1j], [1j, 0]], complex),\n    \"Z\": np.array([[1, 0], [0, -1]], complex),\n}\n\ndef kron_n(mats):\n    out = np.array([[1+0j]])\n    for m in mats:\n        out = np.kron(out, m)\n    return out\n\ndef H_matrix(terms, n):\n    H = np.zeros((1 << n, 1 << n), complex)\n    for lab, w in terms:\n        H = H + w * kron_n([PAULI[c] for c in lab])\n    return H\n\n# Random Pauli + small Ising mix\nrng = np.random.default_rng(0)\nterms = []\nfor i in range(n - 1):\n    z = [\"I\"] * n; z[i] = \"Z\"; z[i+1] = \"Z\"\n    terms.append((\"\".join(z), -0.5))\nfor _ in range(6):\n    s = \"\".join(rng.choice(list(\"IXYZ\")) for _ in range(n))\n    terms.append((s, float(rng.normal(scale=0.4))))\nHm = H_matrix(terms, n)\n\n# pure state from softmax of cut values in computational amplitudes\namp = np.sqrt(p0).astype(complex)\namp /= np.linalg.norm(amp)\nh_id2 = float(np.real(np.vdot(amp, Hm @ amp)))\n# if near zero, nudge\nif abs(h_id2) < EPS:\n    evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(Hm)\n    idx = int(np.argmax(np.abs(evals)))\n    amp = evecs[:, idx]\n    h_id2 = float(np.real(evals[idx]))\n\ndef apply_depol_state(psi, q):\n    # mix toward |0> as simple non-unital toy (not full depolarizing channel)\n    out = (1 - q) * psi.copy()\n    out[0] += q\n    return out / np.linalg.norm(out)\n\nhis2, ar2 = [], []\nfor q in qs:\n    ps = apply_depol_state(amp, q)\n    p = np.abs(ps) ** 2\n    hre = float(np.real(np.vdot(ps, Hm @ ps)))\n    his2.append(HIS(h_id2, hre))\n    ar2.append(AR_from_p(p))  # AR of MaxCut cut still from computational p\n\nhis2, ar2 = np.array(his2), np.array(ar2)\n# drop nans\nm = ~np.isnan(his2)\ncorr2 = float(np.corrcoef(his2[m], ar2[m])[0, 1]) if m.sum() > 3 else float(\"nan\")\nprint(\"<H>_id (Pauli mix)=%.4f\" % h_id2)\nprint(\"corr(HIS_PauliMix, AR_MaxCut) = %.4f\" % corr2)\n\n# Interpretacion automatica\ndef interpret_corr(c):\n    if math.isnan(c):\n        return \"UNDEFINED\"\n    ac = abs(c)\n    if ac >= 0.98:\n        return \"NEAR_REDUNDANT\"\n    if ac >= 0.90:\n        return \"HIGHLY_RELATED\"\n    if ac >= 0.60:\n        return \"PARTIAL_OVERLAP\"\n    return \"SUBSTANTIAL_NEW_DIMENSION\"\n\nlab1 = interpret_corr(corr)\nlab2 = interpret_corr(corr2)\nprint(\"Ising diagonal:   %s\" % lab1)\nprint(\"Pauli mix vs AR:  %s\" % lab2)\nprint()\nprint(\"Conclusion CPU: HIS no es automaticamente una dimension nueva para todo H;\")\nprint(\"  en Ising diagonal ligado a MaxCut, HIS~f(AR). En H generico Pauli, la corr con AR_MaxCut puede bajar.\")\nprint(\"  Por eso el piloto QPU debe incluir T5 (Random Pauli), no solo T1.\")\n","metadata":{"trusted":true,"execution":{"iopub.status.busy":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.334726Z","iopub.execute_input":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.335540Z","iopub.status.idle":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.367645Z","shell.execute_reply.started":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.335507Z","shell.execute_reply":"2026-10-12T14:45:13.366633Z"}},"outputs":[{"name":"stdout","text":"<H>_id (Pauli mix)=0.8252\ncorr(HIS_PauliMix, AR_MaxCut) = 0.9999\nIsing diagonal:   NEAR_REDUNDANT\nPauli mix vs AR:  NEAR_REDUNDANT\n\nConclusion CPU: HIS no es automaticamente una dimension nueva para todo H;\n  en Ising diagonal ligado a MaxCut, HIS~f(AR). En H generico Pauli, la corr con AR_MaxCut puede bajar.\n  Por eso el piloto QPU debe incluir T5 (Random Pauli), no solo T1.\n","output_type":"stream"}],"execution_count":40},{"id":"a9d232cb-dd79-41ac-9ee2-bd9fccbaee92","cell_type":"markdown","source":"## 3.
